closing.reason: Tried to reach #1264's consequence (the same _over_retired_chunks call holding different partitions from different sessions) and failed. (1) Call sites: _over_retired_chunks is the only reader of retired ledger bounds; its callers are _archive_step (install.sql:5351), retain() (4194) and scripts/archive_partition_whole.sql, all through it; no copy in pgpm_archive/pgpm_hypertable; uninstall drops the schema. The floor via _native_order_key keys only ISO text with a numeric offset (session-invariant) and leaves every other row a candidate. (2) Live on pgpm_prv-15: pgpm._native_bound_key over 14 legacy shapes (SQL/German/Postgres-style renders ending in IST, EST, CST, SAST, BST; offset-less ISO; DMY-shaped; numeric offset; full zone name Asia/Kolkata; T...Z; Julian; 9-digit fractions) from 675 sessions (5 TimeZones x 5 DateStyles x Default/Australia/India x 3 IntervalStyles x extra_float_digits -15/0/3) gave exactly one key per text; _over_retired_chunks over a UTC grid with IST/EST/CST/DMY/zone-name hi chunks gave 1 distinct answer over 180 sessions on head, 2 on base. (3) Settings: the caller's TimeZone, DateStyle and timezone_abbreviations are restored after the call whether set by SET, SET LOCAL in an open transaction, or set_config(...,true) in a DO block, and after an error the function raised and the caller caught. (4) Mutations each put back a part of this defect (session zone, UTC read, DateStyle pin, abbreviation pin); the ACC repro fails only on the session-zone mutant, as expected for a UTC grid. Residue, not claims: an abbreviation absent from Default (WST, SAT, Australia-set only; not produced by tzdata since 2014) now raises from every session, where on base it parsed only in Australia-set sessions and raised in pg_cron's Default one; Default reads a Kolkata or Dublin-written 'IST' as Israel's, deterministically, the documented choice; on PG 18, input prefers the abbreviations of the pinned TimeZone (partition_tz), so on a grid registered in an IST zone 'IST' would not be Israel's as reference.md says, but it would still be the same from every session (not testable here, PG 15 only); set_partition_tz moves where an offset-less legacy bound falls, which is an operator's state change, not session dependence.
